title: Alon's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz
description: Formalizes Alon's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz (1999): if a multivariate polynomial has a nonzero coefficient at a maximal-degree monomial, it cannot vanish on a sufficiently large product grid. Proves the single-variable base case from Mathlib's polynomial root bounds.

overview.historicalContext:
Noga Alon introduced the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz in 1999 as a unifying algebraic tool for combinatorial problems. The result distills the essence of the polynomial method: if a polynomial has a nonzero coefficient at a specific monomial and we evaluate on sufficiently large sets, some evaluation must be nonzero.

The name references Hilbert's Nullstellensatz from algebraic geometry, but the result is fundamentally different: it applies over arbitrary fields (not just algebraically closed) and concerns explicit non-vanishing rather than ideal-variety correspondence. Alon used it to give elegant proofs of the Cauchy-Davenport theorem, permanent bounds, and graph coloring results.

The polynomial method, of which the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz is a cornerstone, has produced major advances in combinatorics, additive number theory, and computer science over the past three decades.
overview.problemStatement:
Formalize Alon's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz:

Let $F$ be a field and $f \in F[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ with $\deg(f) = \sum t_i$. If the coefficient of $\prod x_i^{t_i}$ in $f$ is nonzero, and $S_1, \ldots, S_n \subseteq F$ with $|S_i| > t_i$, then $\exists\, a_i \in S_i$ with $f(a_1, \ldots, a_n) \neq 0$.
overview.text: Formalizes Alon's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz in Lean 4 using Mathlib's multivariate polynomial infrastructure. Proves the single-variable base case and axiomatizes the full multi-variable theorem.
overview.proofStrategy:
The proof of the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz has three main steps:

1. **Polynomial reduction**: For each $i$, let $g_i(x_i) = \prod_{s \in S_i} (x_i - s)$. Reduce $f$ modulo $g_1, \ldots, g_n$ to get a remainder $r$ with $\deg_{x_i}(r) < |S_i|$ for each $i$.

2. **Coefficient preservation**: The monomial $\prod x_i^{t_i}$ has degree $t_i < |S_i|$ in each variable, so it is not affected by the reduction. Thus $r$ has the same nonzero coefficient, so $r \neq 0$.

3. **Grid non-vanishing**: Since $r \neq 0$ and $\deg_{x_i}(r) < |S_i|$, by induction on the number of variables, $r$ (and hence $f$) doesn't vanish on $S_1 \times \cdots \times S_n$.

The single-variable base case uses Mathlib's `card_roots_le_degree`: a nonzero polynomial of degree $d$ has at most $d$ roots. This is fully proved in our formalization.
keyInsights: The single-variable non-vanishing lemma follows directly from Mathlib's polynomial root count bound (card_roots_le_degree)
The Combinatorial Nullstellensatz works over ANY field, not just algebraically closed fields — this distinguishes it from Hilbert's Nullstellensatz
The main formalization barrier is multivariate polynomial division (reducing modulo grid polynomials one variable at a time)
The grid non-vanishing lemma (bounded degree → doesn't vanish on grid) is provable by induction using the single-variable case
The theorem statement uses Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite to convert degree vectors (σ → ℕ) to Finsupp multi-indices (σ →₀ ℕ)

sections.title: Single-Variable Non-Vanishing (Proved)
sections.summary: Proves the base case: a nonzero polynomial of degree $d$ over a field cannot vanish on more than $d$ points. Uses `Polynomial.card_roots_le_degree` from Mathlib.

sections.title: Grid Non-Vanishing (Axiomatized)
sections.summary: States the grid non-vanishing lemma: a nonzero multivariate polynomial with $\deg_{x_i}(f) < |S_i|$ for each $i$ cannot vanish on $S_1 \times \cdots \times S_n$.
sections.mathContext: Provable by induction on the number of variables, using the single-variable case at each step.

sections.title: The Combinatorial Nullstellensatz (Axiomatized)
sections.summary: States Alon's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz with the precise conditions: total degree = $\sum t_i$, nonzero coefficient of $\prod x_i^{t_i}$, and $|S_i| > t_i$.
sections.mathContext: The full theorem combines polynomial reduction (modulo grid polynomials) with the grid non-vanishing lemma.

sections.title: Consequences and Variants (Proved)
sections.summary: Derives the $|S_i| \geq t_i + 1$ variant and the uniform grid specialization, both proved from the axiomatized main theorem.

conclusion.summary: This file formalizes Alon's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz (1999) in Lean 4, proving the single-variable base case from Mathlib's polynomial root bounds and axiomatizing the full multi-variable theorem. With 2 axioms and 3 proved results, it establishes the formal statement of one of combinatorics' most powerful algebraic tools.
conclusion.implications:
**Practical Impact**: The Combinatorial Nullstellensatz is one of the most-cited results in algebraic combinatorics. A formal version enables verified algebraic proofs of combinatorial results in Lean.

**Path to Full Proof**: The main barrier is multivariate polynomial division in Mathlib. The grid non-vanishing lemma could be proved next by induction using the single-variable case.
